text:
The fort has a door now.

It didn't have a door at four o'clock — you were here, you watched her rule that a fort with a door was a house, and houses were for people with nothing to read — and now there's a door, a paperback archway two books deep, and Nova is upside down inside it with her feet flat against the wall and a broken spine open above her face.

"Don't," she says, not looking up. "Whatever your face is doing. I can hear it."

You check. Your face has already decided the fort is good and is a little ahead of you about it. You let it stay ahead. Across the low table the takeout has stopped steaming — three cartons, the good chopsticks, and the one fork, because Astra will not be talked out of the fork — and Astra herself is on the floor with her back to the shelf, dark wrap loose off one shoulder, watching you not answer Nova.

"He's reading the door," Astra says.

"The door is load-bearing."

"The door is the only part that isn't."

The whole goblin comes over sideways in a clatter — Nova righting herself, red eyes up now, the black lipstick catching the lamp, the closest thing to formalwear she owns and she reapplied it for a Tuesday. "Okay, but structurally—"

"Structurally, the fort stands because you leaned three hardcovers against my knee twenty minutes ago and told me to hold still."

"That's called collaboration."

"That's called me."

You cross to the low table and crouch, and you pick up the contested fork, and you hold it out toward Astra — and she doesn't take the fork. She takes two fingers to the front of your shirt instead and pulls, unhurried, until you come down the last foot to the floor with her.

The floor is where dinner is now, apparently. Astra's reaching past you for a carton before you've fully landed, so the pull wasn't about you — or wasn't only — and you put the fork in her hand before she asks for it.

"Thank you," she says, and eats a dumpling with the fork, in front of you, on purpose.

From the fort: "That is a war crime. Chopsticks exist. I laid them out."

"I'm aware of the chopsticks," you say, and you reach into the near carton with your fingers and eat a dumpling with your hand — a third position — and you watch it land: Nova's bark of a laugh out of the paperback archway, one corner of Astra's mouth moving.

"Oh, we're doing anarchy." Nova's already coming out of the fort, book left spine-up on the blanket, crossing the floor to drop in on your other side, so you're between them now. "Cool. Love that for us. Except the fort has a dumpling clause, and the dumpling clause is extremely clear that the goblin who did the labor—"

"Décor," Astra says.

"—the LABOR — eats—"

You put a dumpling in her mouth. Her mouth was open and legislating and the legislation was, functionally, a request for a dumpling, so you grant it, and the rest of the clause dies around a mouthful of pork.

Nova chews. Produces a chopstick from somewhere and points it at you, still chewing.

"That's a bribe," she manages. "That's a documented bribe. Honestly? Strong play. Aggro dumpling diplomacy, I respect it, I'm keeping the receipt." She swallows and settles back against your side like she's claimed a checkpoint. "Clause tabled. But the record shows the goblin got fed first and it was correct."

"It's on the record," Astra says. She's stopped eating. She turns her glass a quarter-turn on the low table, and then another quarter, and you clock it the way you clock weather, and file it to read later.

"Astra." Nova sits up an inch. "You've got a look. That's a whole face."

"I'm choosing a moment." Astra's still watching her own glass. "This isn't it. Eat."

You stack the empty cartons. One dumpling's left in the near carton, marooned by politeness, so you rescue it and cut it into three even pieces with the edge of the fork.

Nova takes her third off your fingers with her chin still on your shoulder. She doesn't eat it right away. Half a beat where her eyes cut to the fort and back, and whatever goes across her face gets folded under the next thing out of her mouth, which is loud: "Okay. Fort motion. Non-negotiable, but I'm calling it a motion so it stays polite." She's already peeling off your side, both hands out, one for you and one for the air where Astra is. "Everybody in. I built the thing. Come see what it's for."

Astra doesn't take the hand yet. She looks at the shelf — one look, quick —

and then she takes the hand, and Nova hauls — Nova has never once hauled gently — and the three of you go down into the fort in a slow avalanche of paperbacks and elbows.

Inside is warmer. The good blanket from the couch is down over the floor of it, and the lamplight comes through the paperback walls in thin gold seams. There's exactly enough room for three if two of them overlap.

You end up on your back. Astra fits along one side of you without being asked; Nova stakes the other, propped on an elbow up over your chest, close enough now that the black lipstick is just her mouth.

"From in here," Astra says, quiet, "it's better." She doesn't say better than what.

"Okay." You find you've got a hand at the small of Nova's back, and you keep it there. "Show me what it's for."

She reaches back over your shoulder, into the deep seam of the fort where the blanket meets the wall, and her hand closes on something that's been waiting there since before dinner. She doesn't pull it out. She holds it where it is and looks at you, then down at whatever's in her fist, then at you again. She opens her mouth. She closes it again.

What comes out of the fist is a paperback, and it's wrecked. The spine's gone white and soft where it's been broken and re-broken, the cover a cheap dragon worn almost featureless, the whole thing swollen with rereading. She sets it down on your sternum like it weighs more than it does.

You lay a hand flat over it.

"Okay, so, don't," she says, fast, both hands already up in her own defense. "Don't do a face. It's not — it's the first one. The first one I ever—" She stops. Comes back lower. "I was fourteen. It's stupid, the prose is genuinely bad, I've reread it eleven times and it does not improve, that's not the—"

Astra has come up on an elbow on your other side to see. She doesn't reach for the book. She reads the margins from where she is — the pen crowding every white edge in a kid's hand, cramped and sure — and the faint light under her skin comes up, and she looks straight at you while it does.

"Read us the part," Astra says. "The one with the corner turned down."

Nova takes the book back off your chest, two hands, careful, and finds the page without hunting for it. She doesn't do a voice. That's the part your attention snags on: no goblin delivery, no bit. She reads it low and plain, the way someone reads a thing they know by heart, and the whole loud machine of her goes quiet around the sentences.

It's not good prose. She was right about that. It's a boy on a wall at the end of everything, holding a sword he doesn't know how to use and deciding to stay anyway — earnest and overwritten and obviously the most important thing that ever happened to somebody. She reads it like it's still the most important thing.

Astra doesn't move, her eyes on Nova's mouth and not the page, the glow still up.

Then Nova's thumb finds the margin and she stops reading out loud. Book flat to her chest. Red eyes down on the pen scrawl there, going nowhere. For a second nobody says anything.

"Fourteen-year-old me put a note here," she says. Quiet. "I'm not reading you the note."

You get a hand into the short hair at the back of her neck.

"Okay," you say. "Not the note."

For a while, nobody moves. Then Astra does — not toward you, away, up and out of the overlap, and the cool where she was is instant. She sits back on her heels at the mouth of the fort. Every motion goes exactly where she means it, nothing fast, nothing wasted.

"Where are you going," Nova mumbles, eyes still shut.

"The shelf." Astra's already up. "Don't move, either of you. I've been building up to this for three days and I'll lose my nerve if you're helpful about it."

You prop up on your elbows to watch her cross the room. There's been something on that shelf for a few days now. You'd half-clocked it, a small pale thing set at eye level, and left it for her. She reaches it and stops, and doesn't pick it up yet. She stands with her back to you, both hands loose at her sides, looking at it.

She picks it up. Turns. Comes back across the room with both hands cupped around something you still can't see, folds down into the fort with more care than the trip needs, and opens her hands over the blanket between the three of you.

It's a leaf. That's the nearest word for it. A single sheet of something thin as paper and not paper, pale, faintly lit from inside like the underside of a cloud with the sun behind it, its edges not quite holding still when you look straight at them. When Astra breathes, it stirs.

You sit up to see it.

"It's a page of the first stuff," she says, and then, because that lands as nothing: "The material everything's made out of, before it's made into anything. There isn't much of it anywhere. This is a piece of mine."

"Astra." Nova's come up on both elbows, red eyes huge, and whatever she was going to say doesn't arrive.

"It holds what you put on it. Not for a long time. Not 'archival.' Forever — the real one." Astra sets a pen down on the blanket beside it, an ordinary ballpoint. Of everything in the room, your eye goes to the pen. "It's blank. I haven't written on it. I didn't want to be the one who decided what it says."

Nova reaches for it — slow, for Nova, both hands, like it might be hot — and stops just short. "Can I."

"You can hold it. It won't tear."

She lifts it onto her two palms, red eyes going over the pale not-paper, and the appraisal she always has ready doesn't come. "Okay," she says, quiet, to the leaf and not to either of you. "Okay. This is the best thing I've ever held."

"Nova. Put it down." A beat. "Not away. Down."

Nova sets the leaf on the blanket, slow, and looks up, and now both of you are looking at Astra instead of the thing she made.

She doesn't deflect it. You've watched her hand the credit off a hundred times — to the object, the room, the fort's east wall — and you can see her decline to do it now. She holds where she is and takes the looking.

The glow comes up under her skin. Where she'd usually catch it and put it away, this time she does nothing at all, and it rises past hiding, the pale of it reaching your face and Nova's, her eyes on you the whole way up.

"I didn't leave it on the shelf because I couldn't choose the words," she says. Slower now, each one set down exactly. "I left it there to find out if either of you would ask me what it was. You didn't. You walked past it eleven times." The corner of her mouth moves. "I counted. I wasn't hurt. I was interested — in whether, if nobody asked, I could ask anyway."

Nova makes a low sound and comes up off her elbows, both hands, already moving, and Astra says "wait." Not sharp. Nova waits, strung tight with it.

"Look at me." Astra's eyes haven't left you. "Not the thing I made. Me. I'd like, for one night, to be the thing that gets picked up instead of the thing everything gets set on."

Your eyes went to her before that sentence finished and they have not come back, so the looking was never going to be the hard part. The hard part is that she asked in words, out loud, which means the answer has to come the same way.

"Yeah," you say. It comes out level. No performance in it. "I see you. You're lit up like something struck and holding your face like you meant to be, and you didn't, and that's the—" You stop, because finishing it would be handing her a joke to hide behind, and she asked you for the exact opposite. "I see you. That's the answer. I'm not looking at the page."

Astra goes completely still. She doesn't answer in words. The glow does it for her, steady and full and finally not hidden from anyone.

Then she looks at Nova, still poised and shaking on both hands where she was told to hold. "Okay," Astra says, and her voice isn't steady. "Okay. Now."

Nova hits the two of you like weather.

Nova lands on you full-length, both hands in your hair, and kisses you like she's been polite for four hours and is finished being polite. Nothing tentative in it — her mouth open on yours, black lipstick be damned, one knee driving down between your legs, and the sound she makes into your mouth is low and greedy.

Your hands are up under the back of her shirt before you've caught up to them, palms flat on the warm run of her spine, and she arches into it like you found a switch she put there herself.

Astra takes the other side of you. Her mouth finds the side of your throat — not a kiss so much as slow pressure, teeth and then tongue, right over the spot where your pulse is making a fool of itself.

"He's already gone," Astra says against your throat. "Both hands, no plan. Nova, look at his hands."

"I felt them." Nova catches your bottom lip in her teeth, grinning. "Ten out of ten hands. Immediate loot." Then she sits up astride your hips and pulls her shirt off over her head, graceless, and there's the green of her in the lamplight, small and strong and unreasonably good. She reaches to move your hand onto her breast and finds it already there.

Astra sits up off your throat, and for a moment the two of them are kneeling over you, looking at each other across your chest — Nova flushed and greedy, Astra lit faintly from inside — and something goes between them, over your sternum, that you're not part of and don't need to be.

Then Astra reaches across and takes Nova's jaw in one hand and kisses her, slow and deliberate, and Nova makes a sound into it and grabs a fistful of Astra's wrap. So that's what you get to do for a while: lie there with a hand on Nova's thigh and a hand on Astra's hip and watch the two women you love kiss each other three inches above your chest like they've got all night. Which, you're being reminded, they do.

"Okay," you manage, and that's the whole sentence. Your body has made its opinion loudly clear against the inside of your jeans, and neither of them has so much as looked.

Nova breaks off first. "Right?" she says to Astra, wet-mouthed and delighted. "Every time. Look at him."

You give them something better to look at than your face.

You get an arm around her back and sit up into her, and it puts her right where you want her; you turn your head and take her nipple in your mouth. The sound she makes stops being for Astra's benefit. Her hand comes up hard against the back of your skull, holding you there. "Oh — okay," she says, and for once there's nothing in it but the fact of it.

Astra has your shirt up and off in the middle of that — you register it as cool air and then the warm length of her against your bare back, her hands coming around to your belt and taking their own sweet time with it. Her mouth rests at the top of your spine. "Don't rush," she says, to you or Nova or the room. "We're not rushing anything."

You let her have the belt. The moment the buckle gives, you move — an arm hard around Nova, a knee braced under you, and you roll and bring her over with you. Astra's hands leave your back; her laugh follows you down. And it's Nova underneath now, blinking up, startled and pleased and briefly out of things to say, your hand spread open between her shoulder blades where you caught her. You hold there a second, over her, close enough that she has to feel you decide what happens next.

Behind you, cloth gives. You look back: Astra has the wrap off at last, dropped somewhere in the dark, kneeling up bare, the low light in her coming to the surface where your eyes land. She doesn't cover it and she doesn't deflect. She holds still under your eyes and does not look away.

She doesn't wait to be asked twice. She comes to your side, one hand flat on your back, the other finishing what it started at your belt — takes the jeans down and off, and you kick free of them. Now there's nothing left on you at all, and she looks at that too, unbothered and pleased.

When you come back down over her, your cock is bare against the crease of Nova's hip — her bottoms shoved low but still on — and she makes a low sound like she's been waiting all evening for exactly that. She gets a hand down between you and takes hold of you, greedy and certain, and your breath goes rough.

Astra sets her chin on your shoulder and watches Nova's hand move on you, close enough that her breath shifts against your neck. "Slower," she tells Nova. "We're going to make this take all night." And Nova, for once, does what she's told.

You take the slow way down Nova's body, an inch at a time — mouth and then teeth at her ribs, her stomach, the sharp jut of her hip — until you can hook her bottoms down and off and drop them past the edge of the blanket. She lifts to help you, then swears at how long you're taking.

You settle between her thighs and put your tongue to her clit — one long stroke, and then another — and Nova's swearing goes high and helpless, both hands dropping to your head.

Above you, Astra takes Nova's face in both hands and kisses the noise out of her. You catch the moan more than hear it — the sound traveling down the length of her to where your mouth is working.

Nova gets one hand knotted in your hair and the other up in Astra's, holding on to both of you like the floor's tilting under her. You can feel it starting to climb in her — the shake coming into her thighs against your ears, her hips no longer waiting for you but chasing. So you ease off again, just to hear what she calls you for it.

Astra lifts her mouth off Nova's, looks down the length of her to where you're working, and says it for her. "Now."

So you stop teasing. You put your mouth back on her — flat, hard, no more give in it — and work her straight over the edge you've been holding her at. Nova comes with her thighs locked around your head and your name coming out of her broken in half, and you feel every second of it against your mouth.

Astra watches the whole thing happen with open appetite, one hand on Nova's stomach to feel it go through her. Then she looks at you — at your mouth wet from Nova, at the state the rest of you is in, still untouched and aching.

She gets a hand around the back of your neck and draws you up off Nova and around to her, Nova gone boneless and laughing weak somewhere below you. "My turn to be greedy," Astra says, and puts her mouth on yours so you taste what she's been watching.

Astra lies back and pulls you down over her. She guides you in with one hand, the other at the small of your back drawing you the rest of the way, and then you're deep in her — and she makes a sound you've never heard her make: low, undone.

Your rhythm breaks and comes back rougher than you mean it, all the patience you'd been running on gone out of it, and you press your mouth to her throat to keep quiet — and don't.

Nova's come back to herself enough to push up on one arm and watch the two of you with open delight — and then she can't just watch. She tucks herself against Astra's side, gets a hand into her hair, and sets her mouth to Astra's ear to tell her, in detail, exactly how good she looks taking you.

Astra goes first. You feel it happen — the clench, the shake, your name this time where the instruction used to be — and it takes you with her, the ache finally paying out, and you're gone too, forehead down on her collarbone, wrung right out. And it's Nova who finds words first, soft and wrecked and pleased with you both. "There it is," she says. "That's the whole thing, right there."

It's a while before anybody says anything worth the effort of saying. The three of you come apart slow and rearrange into a heap with no dignity in it and no wish for any — Astra on her back getting her breath, you half on her and half on the blanket, Nova draped over the both of you like she's staking a claim. The lamplight comes soft through the paperback walls. The fort's still standing.

Nova talks first. "Somebody is going to have to bring me a sandwich," she informs the paperback ceiling, with enormous dignity. "I've done a lot of work here tonight." Astra huffs a laugh, and you feel it move through her where your head's gone down on her chest.

Somewhere up near your head is the leaf Astra gave you — that single blank sheet of the first stuff, the pen uncapped beside it where it got set down. None of you reaches for it. It can stay blank a while longer; there's no rush on the first word, and anyway your hands are full.

You lie there in the wreck of the fort and take stock: the ache gone quiet, a grin on your face you can feel but never chose, Nova's dead weight, Astra's heartbeat under your ear coming slowly down. Your body's gotten here a long way ahead of you, and for once it hasn't got a single note of complaint to file.
